Title: Operating envelope of Haber-Bosch process design for power-to-ammonia $ ^{\dagger} $

Abstract: The power-to-ammonia concept allows for the production of ammonia, one of the most produced inorganic chemicals, from air, water and (renewable) electricity. However, power-to-ammonia requires flexible operation for use with a directly intermittent renewable energy supply. In this paper, we systematically analyse the operating envelope for steady-state operation of the three bed autothermic Haber–Bosch reactor system for power-to-ammonia by pseudo-homogeneous model. Operational flexibilities of process variables, hydrogen intake and ammonia production flexibilities are analysed, along with maximum and minimum possible changes in recycle load and recycle to feed ratio for the following process variables: reactor pressure, inert gas percentage in synthesis loop, NH₃ concentration, H₂-to-N₂ ratio, total flow rate and feed temperature. Among the six process variables, inert gas fraction and H₂-to-N₂ ratio provided very high flexibilities, ca. 255% operational flexibility for Ar, up to 51 to 67% flexibility in hydrogen intake, and up to 73% reduction and 24% enhancement in ammonia production. However, a decrease in ammonia production by H₂-to-N₂ ratio significantly increases recycle load. Besides inert gas fraction and H₂-to-N₂ ratio, the total mass feed flow rate is also significant for minimum hydrogen intake and ammonia production.

Model: Pseudo-homogeneous Haber–Bosch process
Laws:
(2) [constitutive] The exchanger effectiveness relation computes the shell-side outlet temperature from the two inlet temperatures.
(3) [balance] The material balance computes the change in reactant conversion through a catalyst bed from the ammonia formation rate and inlet reactant flow.
(4) [balance] The energy balance computes the temperature change through a catalyst bed from reaction heat release, mass flow, and heat capacity.
(5) [constitutive] The modified Temkin rate expression computes ammonia formation from nitrogen, hydrogen, and ammonia activities, with the equilibrium and reverse-reaction terms setting the net rate.
(6) [balance] The mixer material balance computes the reactant conversion after quenching from the bed and quench reactant flows.
(7) [balance] The mixer energy balance computes the post-quench temperature from the bed-out and quench-stream enthalpy contributions.

States (computed by the ODEs):
- X_{r,b}: reactant conversion in catalyst bed b
- T_{b}: temperature of the fine catalyst particles in bed b

Inputs (variables no law computes):
- T_{t_{in}}: tube-side inlet temperature (catalyst bed 3 outlet)
- T_{s_{in}}: shell-side inlet temperature
- R_{NH_3,b}: ammonia formation rate in catalyst bed b
- \dot{n}_{r,b_{in}}: molar flow rate of reactant entering catalyst bed b
- \dot{m}_{b_{in}}: Mass flow rate entering catalyst bed b.
- a_{N_2}: Nitrogen activity coefficient.
- a_{H_2}: Hydrogen activity coefficient.
- a_{NH_3}: Ammonia activity coefficient.
- X_{r,b_{out}}: Reactant conversion at the bed outlet.
- \dot{n}_{r,b_{out}}: Reactant molar flow rate at the bed outlet.
- \dot{n}_{r,q_{in}}: Reactant molar flow rate entering the quench.
- \dot{m}_{b_{out}}: Mass flow rate leaving the bed.
- T_{b_{out}}: Temperature of the stream leaving the bed.
- \dot{m}_{q_{in}}: Mass flow rate entering the quench.
- T_{q_{in}}: Temperature of the stream entering the quench.

Model-wide assumptions:
- The reactor is represented by a pseudo-homogeneous model.
- Heat losses are ignored.
- The reactor system is isobaric.
- The temperature gradient inside catalyst pellets is negligible.
- Gas mixing in the mixer is ideal and instantaneous.
- During normal operation, 27.79 mol% of NH₃ is carried along with the recycled unused reactants.

answer.description: This pseudo-homogeneous model represents a three-bed autothermic Haber–Bosch reactor system for ammonia synthesis in a power-to-ammonia process. It predicts reactant conversion and catalyst-particle temperature through the beds, supporting analysis of the steady-state operating envelope and resulting ammonia production. The model combines modified Temkin reaction kinetics with bed material and energy balances, heat exchange, and quench mixing.
